Name: AliveNpcs Economy
Author: GatoAsmatico907
Description:
[left][center][b]💰 AliveNpcs Economy

[/b][/center]
Your conversations with the villagers now move real gold, real items and real debts

An addon for AliveNpcs,

In AliveNpcs you can haggle with Pierre, agree on a price, and hear him say "deal". But that's where it ends. The gold never leaves your wallet, the seeds never reach your inventory, and tomorrow nobody remembers the arrangement.

This addon closes that gap. You talk exactly the same way — free text, no menus, no JSON — and when the two of you settle on something, the game obeys.

[center][b][size=5]PRESS F10.[/size][/b][/center]


─────────────────────────────────────────────


How It Works

You talk → the AI decides → the code validates → the game changes → the villager remembers

The AI never touches your save. Alongside its reply it returns a structured intent, and this mod checks the item, the quantity, the price band, your wallet, the villager's stock and their own cash before executing anything. If something doesn't add up, nothing happens and the AI is told why, so it can push back naturally on its next line.

You never see a single line of JSON. You see Pierre talking.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


✨ What You Can Actually Do


Trading and Haggling

* Negotiate price in plain conversation — counter-offers, discounts, walking away.
* Villagers sell only what they actually have in stock, and pay only with money they actually have.
* Buy on credit: take the goods now, a debt is created for the price.
* Sell your own crops, fish, ore and forage to whoever deals in them.


Barter

* No gold needed. "I haven't got 200g — would five fish do it?"
* Some villagers would rather have goods than coins. One of them refuses money entirely.
* Needs a little gold on top to even out? The AI can combine a swap and a payment in the same deal.
* Value guards on both sides: a villager can be generous, but neither of you can be robbed.


Credit and Debt

* Take goods now and pay later, on the terms you agreed out loud.
* Deadlines only exist if you actually negotiate one. No invented due dates.
* Partial payments, renegotiation ("give me a few more days"), and forgiveness.
* Paying up builds trust. Ignoring an agreed deadline costs you.
* No deadline agreed? Then nothing penalises you — but their patience wears thin, and a villager who has been waiting three seasons is much harder to talk into anything.


Standing Agreements

* Some deals aren't gold-for-goods. "I'll give you 50% of the harvest profit" has no fixed amount and no fixed date.
* Those are recorded as free-form agreements the villager keeps bringing up until you settle them.
* The game doesn't enforce them — it's between the two of you, and you pay when you're ready.
* Leave one rotting long enough and they stop extending you credit. No deadline was broken; your word just stopped meaning much.


Commissions and Gifts

* "Bring me 10 Copper Ore and I'll pay you 300g" becomes a real quest in your journal.
* A villager can hand you an item or gold for free when their character would genuinely do it.
* Gift limits are tighter than trade limits by design — that's the only path where value moves for nothing.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🏪 Every Trader Is a Different Trader


Pierre, Marnie, Willy, Clint, Linus, Gus and Robin each have their own stock, cash, catalogue — and their own way of doing business.

* Pierre is a shopkeeper first and a neighbour second. He pushes for the better price, rewards loyalty with a real discount, and will sell on credit to someone whose word has held up.
* Clint would rather talk about ore than money. He prefers a good piece of metal to a coin, and quotes a harder price to someone he's never dealt with.
* Linus lives outside the money economy on purpose. He does not take gold at all — with him, you trade or you go home.
* Willy names a fair price and doesn't move far from it, but he'll happily take fish instead.
* Marnie would rather be fair than squeeze you, and softens for anyone good with animals.

Each of them has both a temperament the AI reads and hard rules the code enforces, so a wary trader doesn't just sound wary — he actually charges you more until you've done business together.

They restock daily, only buy what fits their trade, and it all lives in a plain JSON file you can edit without recompiling anything. Villagers who aren't in that file still negotiate normally, just without stock tracking. Nobody was turned into a merchant against their will.


Dynamic Pricing

The asking price moves with friendship (up to 25% off at maximum hearts), scarcity (up to 30% more when the shelf is nearly empty), season (out-of-season seeds cost more, using the game's real crop data), and familiarity.

How far a villager will come down is part of who they are. But the AI never sets the range. Generous discounts are allowed. Absurd prices are not.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


📖 The Village Ledger — press F10


Debts, deadlines, agreements, standing and stock used to be invisible: you only knew you owed Pierre 250g if he happened to mention it.

The ledger is organised by person, not by record type — because the question you actually ask is "how do I stand with Pierre?"

Pick someone from the list and you get their portrait, their trade, their friendship hearts and their trade standing side by side. Those two can diverge, and that's the point: you can be Pierre's friend and still a deadbeat.

* Debts — how much, to whom, how many days left, and whether they've already given you more time. Colour-coded, with a badge you can read at a glance: Overdue, Due soon, Paid, Forgiven.
* Agreements — the free-form ones, how long they've been sitting, how much you've paid against them.
* Standing — deals closed, gold moved, loans repaid, days overdue, errands delivered or dropped.
* Stock — what that trader has today, with the real item icons.

The seven traders are always listed. Any other villager appears only once something exists between you — ask a favour of Abigail and her card creates itself.

Fully localised: English, Português Brasileiro, Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Tiếng Việt. It follows your game language and falls back to English for anything else.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🧠 Memory That Feeds Back


Every confirmed transaction becomes context for the next conversation.

* Per-villager history: what you bought, what you owe, what you promised.
* Commercial standing, kept separate from friendship.
* Notable deals are also fed into AliveNpcs' own gossip system, so a big transaction can become village talk, a letter, or a story arc.


The AI Looks For A Way Round

Refusing is easy and boring. If you're short, a trader is told to look at what else is on the table:

"I can't just hand you 500g. But I'll buy those 20 trout off you for 700g — does that solve it?"

And that trade actually happens.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🔒 Protection Against AI Hallucination


This was the hardest part to get right, and it's the reason the mod is safe to use.

* Memory only records what the code confirmed. If the AI says it gave you 1000g and execution failed, the fact does not exist.
* A deal is a package. All the actions of one turn are validated together — half a deal never executes.
* You never pay for nothing. If a villager would only take your gold without handing anything over and without a debt to settle, the whole deal is refused and your money stays put. A debt does not count as your side of it: being put in debt is not receiving something.
* Transactions are ordered so the step that can fail happens before the irreversible one, with rollback behind it.
* Actions run on the game thread, never in parallel with the game loop.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🛠️ Bonus: Muted Villager Fix


When the AI provider fails — a 503, a timeout, a quota wall — AliveNpcs has already marked the villager as "talked to today" and suppresses their base-game dialogue too. They go silent until tomorrow, without a single word having been exchanged.

This addon detects the failed generation and frees them for another attempt, with vanilla dialogue as a safety net. It can be turned off in the settings.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


📋 Requirements


* Stardew Valley 1.6.15
* SMAPI 4.5.2 or newer
* AliveNpcs 1.5.4 or newer — REQUIRED, this addon does nothing without it
* Generic Mod Config Menu — optional

You need AliveNpcs already working with your own AI provider configured. This addon does not use an API key of its own; it rides on the LLM AliveNpcs is already talking to, so it costs you no extra requests.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


📦 Installation


1. Install SMAPI and get AliveNpcs working first.
2. Extract the AliveNpcsEconomy folder into your Mods folder.
3. Launch the game.

That's it. No files to edit, no other mods to update.

On first launch the mod generates its config and inserts one field into AliveNpcs' response schema (assets/prompts/evaluate_response.txt). This is done automatically, a backup is saved as evaluate_response.txt.bak-aura in the same folder, and it's reapplied if an AliveNpcs update overwrites it. Without that field the AI agrees to deals in conversation and nothing happens.

To check it's working, type economy_status in the SMAPI console. You want "Economy layer active: True".


─────────────────────────────────────────────


⚙️ Configuration


Every system can be switched off on its own through GMCM or config.json: trading, barter, gifts, debts, agreements, commissions, villager inventories, dynamic pricing, standing, economic memory, real money transfers, real item transfers.

Safety limits are all adjustable: maximum transaction value, maximum quantity, price multipliers, barter ratios, maximum debt per villager and overall, gift caps, daily transaction limits, quest rewards.

There is no minimum friendship required for credit by default. Whether a villager trusts you is the AI's call, made from the conversation — not a number gate. Raise it in the settings if you'd rather have the hard rule.

assets/npc_profiles.json holds each trader's stock, cash, catalogue and temperament. Edit it freely — no recompiling.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🖥️ Console Commands


For testing without spending AI requests, every action runs through the same validation pipeline the AI uses:

    economy_status                mod state
    economy_stock Pierre          stock, cash and prices
    economy_item Potato Seeds 20  real item id, base price, accepted range
    economy_prompt Pierre          the exact context the AI receives
    economy_ledger                real transactions stored in the save
    economy_debts                  open debts
    economy_rep Pierre            commercial standing
    economy_demo                  fill the save with an example history
    economy_trade Pierre 20 200 buy Potato Seeds
    economy_run Willy barter give_item=Bait give_quantity=20 receive_item=Sardine receive_quantity=5
    economy_restore_template      undo the prompt schema change


─────────────────────────────────────────────


🤝 Compatibility


AliveNpcs.dll is never modified — not one byte.

This addon uses AliveNpcs' public addon API (RegisterDynamicPromptBlock and InjectGossip) plus two Harmony patches to read the AI's structured response, which is the one thing the API doesn't expose. Two further optional patches handle the muted villager fix and can be disabled in the settings.

If a future AliveNpcs update changes those internals, the addon logs a warning and switches off only the economy layer. AliveNpcs keeps working normally.

Everything AliveNpcs already does — dialogue, personalities, memory, gossip, letters, drama, story arcs, festivals, scenes — is untouched.


─────────────────────────────────────────────


⚠️ Preview Release


This is an early public build. It works, but be aware:

* No multiplayer support.
* Not every action has been exercised through the AI yet.
* Back up your save before using it.

If you report a bug, please include your SMAPI log, the villager's name, what you typed, and what you expected to happen.


🌐 Translations welcome

The mod ships in 7 languages. If yours is missing, or a line reads badly, the whole interface lives in plain JSON files under i18n/ — send me a corrected one and it goes in.

[/left]
